title: Arizona State hockey player hospitalized after collapsing during outdoor workout
content:
An Arizona State men’s hockey player collapsed during an outdoor workout Thursday morning and remains hospitalized, according to a statement released by the university Sunday afternoon.

Chris Fiscus, vice president of ASU media relations, declined to name the student-athlete due to privacy laws.

“The university offers its support for the student-athlete, their family and all of our student-athletes during this difficult time,” Fiscus’ statement read.

Fiscus declined to clarify if the workout was sanctioned by the team. NCAA rules allow college hockey teams to start formal activities as soon as classes have started, and ASU began its fall semester on Thursday.

Tempe Fire Medical Rescue sent crews to 400 S. Rural Road, the address for Sun Angel Stadium, at 8:31 a.m. Thursday after receiving a report of a “heat-related illness.” A patient was treated there and transported to a nearby hospital, according to the fire department.

The average temperature in the Phoenix area that day was 92.5 degrees, according to the National Weather Service, and an extreme heat warning was in effect all week. The high temperature reached 106 degrees that afternoon.

This is a developing story and will be updated.
